title: Irving Mills, Moe Gale and the 'Minnie the Moocher' arrangement
summary: Mills brought songs for his publishing house and had Mitchell Parrish write lyrics to 'Willie the Weeper'; the first arrangement fell flat.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And Mills got involved with the band, and Mills started to... I don't know how he got involved with the band. But anyway, he was like a hustling guy. He had a music publishing company. So he was interested in us because of his music publishing. So he gave us different songs to do.
And we got into some kind of controversy with Gale. See, Gale was the man...
Moe Gale. Moe Gale was running...

See, Moe Gale was one of the people who owned the Savoy, and Buchanon was there and another guy... But Moe Gale had the biggest interest. His father had a company called a holding company. And Moe Gale started working out deals with Calloway...

Well, he worked out the deals to go in the theatres. See, for a short length of time after Cab came into the band, we got the chance to go to the Cotton Club. So when we got in the Cotton Club, we started broadcasting. And that's when we got involved with "Minnie The Moocher." See, Irving Mills got ahold of a song that was a public domain. Anybody could take it and put lyrics to it. The name of the song was "Willie The Weeper." So he got Mitchell Parrish to write the lyrics to "Minnie The Moocher."

Mitchell Parrish was a lyrics writer, and he wrote the lyrics to "Minnie the Moocher." So we got... I wish I could think of the guy's name that he got to make this arrangement. This guy is now a big-time arranger in New York. He used to arrange for the Mills Brothers... Because Mills had the Mills Brothers... And he got him to make this arrangement. We played this arrangement, but we
just didn't dig the arrangement. It didn't seem to fit "Minnie The Moocher."
